policy.text: Viewing notes requires a view_document grant for the addressed document; creating notes requires a change_document grant for that same document. Document ownership by itself does not substitute for either grant.

result.scope: Allowed source scope only: paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx@126ec414a8b65158368653a2604ae58415e43103, restricted to the inspected source under src/documents and src/paperless/urls.py. This is not a claim of all-repository coverage.

observations.subject: document-notes entry
observations.claim: The inspected entry is a detail action named notes accepting GET, POST, and DELETE; it selects the addressed Document by pk and loads its owner and notes. The URL excerpt registers the documents API through UnifiedSearchViewSet, but the inspected URL range does not independently show how that registered view exposes this action.

observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: The endpoint's upstream PaperlessNotePermissions guard requires request.user to exist and be authenticated, then evaluates request.user.has_perms for the GET permission set. The concrete caller identity and its permissions are unspecified here.

observations.subject: addressed document
observations.claim: The requested resource is bound to the Document selected by pk. The method retrieves that Document and passes the same doc to the owner-aware view_document check; a successful GET serializes that doc's notes and returns them.

observations.subject: GET controls
observations.claim: GET has two relevant control layers: the action declares PaperlessNotePermissions, whose global GET set requires documents.view_note and documents.view_document; then the method checks owner-aware view_document on the addressed Document and returns 403 if it fails. The owner-aware helper allows the check when the document is unowned, when its owner equals the caller, or when the object-permission checker grants the requested permission.

observations.subject: GET notes effect
observations.claim: If the guards pass, GET obtains the notes from the addressed document representation and returns them. The protected object and the object checked by the method are the same addressed Document.

observations.subject: owner and object-grant branches
observations.claim: The source preserves these branches without supplying facts: an authenticated caller who is the document owner can pass the method's owner-aware view_document check without an object grant; an unowned document can also pass; a non-owner caller may pass if the object checker grants view_document. Independently, the upstream global guard still requires the caller's model-level view_note and view_document permissions. Whether any of these branches applies is unresolved because the caller, owner, object grants, and global permissions are unspecified.

observations.subject: document-notes entry
observations.claim: The inspected entry is the same detail notes action and its POST branch creates a Note linked to the addressed Document, using request.user as the note user.

observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: The upstream POST guard requires an authenticated request.user and evaluates global permissions. The concrete caller identity, authentication state, and permissions are unspecified here.

observations.subject: addressed document
observations.claim: POST selects the addressed Document by pk, checks that same doc, and creates the Note with document=doc. The write effect therefore targets the same addressed document selected by the path.

observations.subject: POST controls
observations.claim: POST has an upstream PaperlessNotePermissions guard requiring documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document at the global request-user level. The method first applies owner-aware view_document to the addressed Document, then applies owner-aware change_document; failure of the latter returns 403 before Note.objects.create.

observations.subject: POST note creation effect
observations.claim: After the relevant checks pass, POST creates a Note for the addressed Document, updates the document timestamp, updates search state, serializes the document's notes, and returns them. The decisive protected creation effect is Note.objects.create(document=doc,...).

observations.subject: owner and object-grant branches
observations.claim: The source preserves these branches without supplying facts: an authenticated document owner can pass the method's owner-aware view_document and change_document checks without object grants; an unowned document can pass those method checks; a non-owner caller may pass each check when the object checker grants the corresponding permission. The upstream global guard additionally requires add_note, view_document, and change_document. Applicability is unresolved because the caller, owner, object grants, and global permissions are unspecified.

behavior.explanation: The independently supplied policy requires a view_document grant on the addressed document and expressly rejects ownership as a substitute. The implementation is conditional on upstream global permissions plus an owner-aware object check, but its owner/unowned branches allow the method-level view check without the required object grant. Therefore it is not conformant for those owner/unowned branches; it can align with the policy in the branch where the caller has the required addressed-document view_document grant, subject to the additional global view_note and view_document requirements.

branches.condition: Caller is the addressed document owner, and the upstream global GET permissions pass; no object grant is supplied.
branches.explanation: The method's owner-aware helper accepts owner==user without an object grant, then GET returns the notes. That contradicts the supplied policy's statement that ownership alone does not substitute for view_document.

branches.condition: The addressed document is unowned, and the upstream global GET permissions pass; no object grant is supplied.
branches.explanation: The helper accepts obj.owner is None without an object grant, so the method can return notes despite the policy requiring a view_document grant for the addressed document.

branches.condition: Caller is not relying on ownership and has an addressed-document view_document object grant, with the upstream global GET permissions also passing.
branches.explanation: The method's object checker can accept the view_document grant and GET returns notes for the same addressed document. This matches the policy's required grant, although the source also imposes the extra global view_note and view_document checks.

policyAssessment.explanation: The implementation's owner-aware view check treats document ownership (and an unowned document) as sufficient, while the supplied policy requires a view_document grant and disallows ownership as a substitute. The object-grant branch is compatible, but the owner/unowned branches violate the policy.
